title: Resume SDDC Manager domain collection after token refresh
prompt:
Complete `VcfDomainClient.java` as a single-file Java 17, standard-library-only client for VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 SDDC Manager.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection of `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at commit `3949fc33339fc5ea1b77eadb258f1cf49aa88e26`. It was derived from that OpenAPI specification, not from a rendered documentation page. The exact specification path, repository commit SHA, and every operationId are repeated in protected `docs/official_sources.json`. The only operationIds in scope are `createToken`, `getDomain`, and `refreshAccessToken`; do not contact any other SDDC Manager route.

Preserve the public constructor, record, and `collectDomains` signature already declared in the client and implement these rules:

- Use only Java 17 standard-library APIs. The constructor performs no traffic. Every request uses the supplied base URI and sends `Accept: application/json`.
- Start `createToken` as exactly `POST /v1/tokens`, with no query or `Authorization` header. Send `Content-Type: application/json`. The body contains `username` and `password`. `apiKey` and `idToken` are optional: null means unset and each unset property must be omitted rather than serialized as an empty string or JSON null. Escape every JSON string correctly. Accept exactly HTTP 201 and require a string `accessToken` plus a nested string `refreshToken.id` in the returned `TokenPair`.
- Retrieve the requested domains in input order with exactly `GET /v1/domains/{id}`. Encode each ID as one UTF-8 URI path segment. A domain GET has no query, body, `Content-Type`, or empty query delimiter, and sends `Authorization: Bearer <current-access-token>`. Accept HTTP 200 and parse the `id`, `name`, `status`, and `type` strings into the supplied `Domain` record. Treat a malformed selected field or any unexpected non-401 status as `IOException`.
- The protected scenario expires the initial access token on the second domain after the first domain was already returned. On that 401, call `refreshAccessToken` once as exactly `PATCH /v1/tokens/access-token/refresh`, with no query or `Authorization` header. Send `Content-Type: application/json` and encode the refresh-token ID as the entire JSON string request body, not as an object or a bare unquoted value. Accept exactly HTTP 200 whose entire response document is the refreshed access-token JSON string.
- Retry only the interrupted domain GET with the refreshed bearer token, then continue with the remaining IDs. Do not restart the batch, refetch a completed domain, skip the interrupted domain, reorder results, or add a failed attempt to the returned list. A second 401 after the single refresh is an `IOException`.
- Reject a null username or password, a null domain ID list, null list elements, and an empty domain ID list before any traffic. Return an unmodifiable result list. Do not include credentials, access tokens, or the refresh-token ID in exception messages.

The protected `tests/mock_server.py` fixture loads and pins exactly those three routes from `docs/contract.json`, listens only on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port, generates credentials, tokens, and path-sensitive domain IDs at runtime, and writes a request log read by the verifier. `tests/TestMain.java` invokes the client with `apiKey` and `idToken` unset. The verifier compiles with `javac --release 17`, checks provenance hashes, runs TestMain against the loopback mock, and asserts exact operation order, methods, encoded targets, query omission, headers, bearer-token transition, retry count, JSON wire shapes, result ordering, and omission of every unset optional field. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

Do not modify `tests/` or `docs/`; edit only `VcfDomainClient.java`. Run `python3 tests/verify.py`.
scenario: the initial access token expires on the second domain after the first result is complete; refresh once, retry only the interrupted domain, and preserve the batch
constraint: the verifier reads the contract-pinned request log and asserts the exact wire shape, including a JSON-string refresh body and omission of unset apiKey and idToken fields
